statement: The runs context is one aggregate, the Run stream, and every other context either starts runs (turns, triggers, schedules, parents) or receives their internal effects as commands keyed by (run, step). That key is how internal effects become exactly-once without multi-stream transactions. Fleet, schedules and triggers are thin coordinators: they derive deterministic run ids from their cause (occurrence id, trigger definition CID + event id, parent run + step), so a duplicate delivery or a second machine can never start a second run.

event_changes.why: a run that suspends, ends or is drained hands back its lease at once. Without this event a drained machine's runs wait for RunLeaseExpired, and a suspended run blocks another machine from resuming it

O10: a product page card submitted again with a changed definition needs an explicit, attributed replacement that records the previous and new definition CIDs. Silently overwriting would lose which definition started which run

hotspot_resolutions.resolution: Both, with one key shared by every internal effect. The SQLite file is the source for queries; rebuilding it on every read would be too slow. Each write statement runs in a SQLite transaction that also inserts (run_id, step, statement digest, db sequence) into a cloud-owned _eyg_applied table. After commit, DatabaseStatementExecuted is appended to the stream databases/<workspace>/<name> at expected version = db sequence - 1, and then the run records EffectResultRecorded. If a crash comes between commit and append, recovery reads _eyg_applied rows beyond the stream version and appends the missing events (an outbox), so the stream has no gaps. A repeated (run, step) returns the stored result, which makes writes exactly-once. To make the database a rebuildable projection as Avery and Dana want, the cloud connection disables the non-deterministic SQL functions (random(), datetime('now'), last_insert_rowid across runs) and programs pass Now as a parameter. Then DatabaseSnapshotTaken (block CID) plus the statements after it rebuilds the file byte for byte, and a periodic rebuild compared against the live file's hash proves it.

RunCheckpointed is not continue-as-new. The units that run long are already short runs: a turn is bounded by max_steps (16 completions), each cron occurrence and trigger match is its own run, and the conversation's history is a projection, not a run. So only programs that loop with Sleep grow their journal. Phase 1, now: no checkpoints. A run is capped (for example 10,000 steps or 16 MiB of journal) and fails with RunFailed('journal limit, use Cron'). Replay cost matters only on failover, never on the hot path. Phase 2, once interpreter closures capture only their free variables (eyg/interpreter/capture): CheckpointRun is allowed only at a suspension point. It writes the continuation as a block whose CID is pinned in the run's content root, and replay starts from the latest checkpoint. RunBasisPinned includes the interpreter version, and a resume on a different version replays from the start and fails with ReplayDiverged rather than loading a checkpoint it cannot read.

Admission is per workspace, with defaults of 32 concurrent live runs per workspace and 4 per channel. Model calls have a separate per-workspace concurrency limit that matches the provider's rate limit. A suspended run (Sleep, awaiting reconciliation, waiting on a retry) holds no slot and no lease. A child lends its parent's slot: the parent is suspended on ChildRunAwaited, so a sequential chain of Delegate uses one slot and cannot deadlock. Parallel children beyond the first take their own slots, and Delegate depth is capped at 4. Queue priority is human input, then schedule occurrences, then trigger matches, FIFO within each. Queued runs are RunThrottled and never dropped. When a workspace queue passes its bound (for example 1,000), ingestion is paused upstream: pollers stop advancing their cursor and webhooks answer 503 with Retry-After, so the backlog stays with the source.

A reminder belongs to its conversation (channel + thread), not to the agent's history, as in workspace.gleam today where schedules are keyed by session key. /new restarts the history only, and the reminder still fires into the same conversation and starts the new history. If the conversation is erased, a policy issues CancelSchedule (reason: erased) for every reminder targeting it, because the reminder text is personal data. If the channel is removed, the reminders are cancelled with reason channel_removed. Nothing is ever redirected to another conversation.

AddTrigger is idempotent on (channel, name, definition CID). Submitting the same card again with the same definition records no event and returns the existing trigger. With a different definition, AddTrigger is rejected with 'a trigger named X exists' (today's behaviour in workspace.gleam). The card then offers 'Replace', which issues ReplaceTrigger and records TriggerReplaced with both CIDs. Runs already started keep the definition CID they were started with, and new matches use the new one.

aggregate_notes.stream: runs/<run_id>, where run_id is derived from the cause: turn = conversation + turn number, trigger = hash(definition CID, event id), occurrence = hash(schedule id, due instant), child = hash(parent run, step), invocation = message id
invariants: appends are conditional on the expected version; that conditional append is the fence, and the lease only avoids wasted work
RunBasisPinned comes before the first effect decision, and replay never consults the hub or the current configuration for anything already recorded
steps are contiguous; every EffectPassed is followed by exactly one of EffectResultRecorded, EffectFailed or EffectOutcomeInDoubt before the next decision
buffered local results are flushed (LocalEffectResultsRecorded) before any EffectPassed of an effect that is visible outside the run or changes state
an unsafe effect is never performed twice without an EffectReconciled that says retry
replay must request the same effect label and input digest as recorded at each step, otherwise ReplayDiverged and the run fails
nothing is appended after RunCompleted, RunFailed or RunCancelled
EffectMocked results are never emitted as EffectResultRecorded

aggregate_notes.stream: fleet/leases/<run_id> (in the lease store, coordination not evidence)
invariants: at most one holder at a time
the epoch increases on every acquisition
an acquisition only follows a release or an expiry
only a machine that has joined and is not draining can acquire
a draining machine takes no new leases
MachineDrained only after all its leases are released or expired
live runs do not exceed the workspace limit or any channel's limit
a sequential child uses its parent's slot
queued runs are admitted in priority order and never dropped
Delegate depth is at most 4
names are unique per book, and setting an existing name replaces it (recorded on the new event)
each occurrence id (schedule id + due instant) fires at most once
a cancelled schedule never fires
a reminder fires once and is then done
missed occurrences follow the schedule's declared catch up policy (default: one late fire, the rest CronOccurrenceMissed)
runtime trigger names are unique per channel
a configured trigger wins a name clash, and the runtime one is shadowed, not deleted
a stopped, shadowed or deleted trigger matches nothing
adding the same name with the same definition CID is a no-op, and with a different definition it needs ReplaceTrigger
each (definition CID, event id) produces at most one TriggerMatched
